S2 — MATERIAL FINDING (1): the L4-F1 summary assigns credit redemption to destruction instead of later grant binding. Report lines 156-158 say: "Destroying the source redeems the named credit, or the oldest open one." Actual destruction at packages/core/src/state/inventoryLifecycle.ts:67-86 preserves open credits when a consumption receipt exists and deletes the inventory row; it neither chooses nor redeems a credit. The later start_effect binding chooses the named/oldest credit at activeEffects.ts:4334-4375 and redeems it atomically with effect insertion at :5684-5690. This is also what .16.10.1's implementer report and .16.10.3 S2 describe. Concrete independent reproducer: node_modules/.bin/tsx /tmp/eshyra-704-review/document-claims.mts. Give three canonical blue-sapphire Elemental Gems and use break-gem three times without binding: inventory is destroyed, both earlier credits still have redeemed_effect_id=null, and the final receipt is also unredeemed. Only a subsequent successful start_effect marks the oldest credit redeemed by gem-effect; the second credit stays open. Original /tmp/l4-gem-conservation.mts also passes all four variants at quantities 2 and 3. Source context: magic-item:elemental-gem, vendored SRD p.220, "When you use an action to break the gem, an elemental is summoned"; this source establishes per-unit entitlement, not automatic redemption during software destruction. Authority/impact: owning .16.12 requires accurate finding wording and dispositions; this sentence misstates the mutation owner and lifecycle point of the repaired capability. Sibling check: inspected both credit and final-receipt payment paths and ordinary non-consumption destruction; the latter still voids open credits. Closure: describe binding a grant from the destroyed source as redeeming the named/oldest open credit, with final-receipt fallback when no credit remains. Owner: PR #704 author/audit consolidator. Evidence: exact documentary counterexample plus existing generalized conservation tests; a documentation correction needs no new permanent test or runtime change.

Direct inspection and the exact counterexample are proportionate evidence for this documentary correction.
